what_its_for: Felbamate is a seizure medicine (anticonvulsant) used to treat epilepsy. It is used for adults and children with hard-to-control seizures, especially a severe type called Lennox-Gastaut syndrome. Because of serious risks, it is usually only used when other seizure medicines have not worked.
how_to_take: Take felbamate by mouth with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or milk. Take it at the same times every day to keep a steady level in your body. Shake the liquid form well before each use and measure it carefully with the measuring device that comes with the medicine — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. Swallow tablets whole or you may crush them if needed. Never stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause more seizures.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over time to find the right amount for you. The dose depends on your age, weight, kidney function, and other medicines you take. Adults typically start at 1,200 mg per day divided into 3 or 4 doses, and the dose may go up to 3,600 mg per day. Children (ages 2 and up) are dosed based on body weight. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store felbamate tablets and liquid at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date on the label. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking felbamate, as it can increase dizziness and drowsiness and may worsen side effects. Be careful driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you — it can cause dizziness or blurred vision. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice unless your doctor says it is okay. Do not take any new prescription medicines, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or herbal supplements without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist, as felbamate interacts with many other medicines.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: unusual bruising or bleeding, extreme tiredness or weakness, yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (jaundice), dark urine, pale stools, severe stomach pain, signs of infection such as fever, chills, or sore throat, unusual mood changes, depression, or thoughts of harming yourself. These can be signs of very serious and rare but life-threatening side effects called aplastic anemia (a blood disorder) or liver failure. Also call your doctor if you have a skin rash, trouble sleeping, loss of appetite, weight loss, nausea, vomiting, or if your seizures are getting worse. Because of the serious risks, your doctor will do regular blood tests and liver tests while you are on this medicine.
when_it_works: Felbamate may start to reduce your seizures within a few weeks, but it may take several weeks to a few months to see the full benefit. Do not stop taking it just because you feel it is not working right away. Keep all your follow-up appointments so your doctor can monitor your progress and adjust your dose if needed.
special_populations: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness and confusion, so lower doses may be needed. People with kidney problems may need a lower dose because felbamate is removed from the body through the kidneys. People with liver problems should use felbamate with extreme caution or not at all due to the risk of liver damage. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, talk to your doctor before taking felbamate — seizure control during pregnancy is very important, but the risks and benefits must be carefully weighed. It is not known if felbamate passes into breast milk, so talk to your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Children aged 2 years and older may take felbamate for Lennox-Gastaut syndrome under close medical supervision with careful dose adjustments based on weight.
